newsitem.title: USA: Former Kodak employee denies selling secrets - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Former Kodak employee denies selling secrets - WSJ.

text.p: A former Eastman Kodak employee accused in a lawsuit of selling company secrets denied in a transcript of a secretly taped meeting that he would disclose such information, the Wall Street Journal said Monday.

The transcript details an August discussion in an Atlanta hotel room betweeen Harold Worden, a 28-year Kodak veteran who is now a consultant, and two undercover Kodak representatives posing as Chinese officials seeking to build a film plant, the paper said.

"I'm not in the business of selling secrets. I am not in the business of selling formulas. We're using our basic technologies to help people, and these things that we recommend are not covered by patents, or patents have expired," the paper quoted Worden as saying in the transcript.
The report said Worden went on to say that he had been asked previously to supply a formula for film emulsion and refused.
Kodak sued Worden in November, alleging that potential competitors bought company secrets worth tens of millions of dollars from him.
The paper quoted a Kodak spokesman as saying the company "stands by its initial accusations."
